statement.p: Let A = \{1,2,\ldots, 13\}\text{.} How many subsets of A contain exactly one element (i.e., how many singleton subsets are there)?
How many doubleton subsets (containing exactly two elements) are there?

hint.p: Write these out, or at least start to and look for a pattern.

solution.p: Each of the 13 elements can be in a singleton set, so there are 13 of these.

To count the number of doubletons, not that there are 12 sets that include 1, and then 11 sets that include 2 and not 1, and then 10 that include 3 and not 1 or 2, and so on. So you can find 78 by summing the numbers from 1 to 12.
